title: Kick-off call — scoring rubric

dimensions.title: Pre-Call Preparation
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach demonstrate they reviewed the sales notes BEFORE the call? Do they reference the client's name, goals, injuries, and context without asking?

bands.label: Elite
bands.criteria: Fully reviewed intake, references goals naturally, no repetition. References specific goals + name + injuries within the first 2 minutes. Uses at least 2 specific details from CRM/notes naturally and in passing. May (but need not) explicitly tell client they don't need to repeat the sales call. Score 10 when delivery is seamless and at least one verbal acknowledgement is present; 9 when otherwise elite without the verbal acknowledgement.

bands.label: Strong
bands.criteria: Clear evidence of preparation in the content (specific goals, pain areas, or context from the sales call surfaced naturally), but with a small gap: a single factual misstep, slightly delayed reference, or one redundant question. Allowing the client to voluntarily share context for relational warmth is NOT a deduction. Score 8 when the gap is minor and clearly outweighed by solid prep; 6 when prep is real but uneven.

bands.label: Mid
bands.criteria: Partial preparation. Some notes used, but several redundant questions or a generic, low-personalization intro. Reads notes mechanically. Reserve for cases where prep is visibly thin, not for cases where prep is solid but the coach didn't verbally announce it.

bands.label: Weak
bands.criteria: Minimal preparation visible. One or two surface references at most; client does most of the context-setting.

bands.label: Fail
bands.criteria: Clearly unprepared. Asks client their name or what brought them here. Completely resets the sale.

positiveSignals: "You don't need to repeat what you told the team…"
negativeSignals: Long pause while searching for information
Multiple redundant logistics questions already covered in sales notes.
notes: Do NOT default to Mid (4–5) simply because the coach did not say "I read your notes." Do NOT drop a strong call to Mid for a single misstep (e.g. wrong city) when the rest of the preparation is solid — score 6–8 instead.

Score on conduct, not on disclosure. Credit preparation when the coach demonstrably uses information that could only have come from the sales notes — specific goals, named pain areas, history details, lifestyle context — even if the coach never explicitly says "I read your notes" or equivalent. The verbal acknowledgement is a positive signal, not a requirement.

Calibration note: Do NOT default to Mid (4–5) simply because the coach did not say "I read your notes." Do NOT drop a strong call to Mid for a single misstep (e.g. wrong city) when the rest of the preparation is solid — score 6–8 instead.

dimensions.title: Rapport & Tone
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does a genuine human connection form? Does the coach adapt their energy to the client? Does the client open up?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Warm, calm, personalized, matches client energy. Conversation is natural and non-scripted. Uses client's name organically. Shares something personal and relevant. Client opens up spontaneously with personal stories.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Friendly but surface-level. Warm and conversational but not deeply personal. Good connection but little emotional mirroring or depth.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Mechanical / scripted feel. Friendly but transactional. Light conversation without real connection.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Cold, rushed, transactional. Skips rapport entirely. No attempt at personal connection. Client gives monosyllabic answers.

dimensions.title: Agenda Framing
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach take control of the call structure upfront and communicate what will happen?

bands.label: Elite
bands.criteria: Clear agenda with explicit time framing AND ≥3 sequenced phases (numbered or natural-language) AND client verbal consent ("sounds good"). Score 5 when all three elements are crisp; 4.5 when the agenda is fully present and sequenced but slightly informal in delivery.

bands.label: Mid
bands.criteria: Agenda mentioned but partial — either time framing missing, fewer than 3 phases, or no client buy-in. Implicit structure rather than intentional framing.

bands.label: Weak
bands.criteria: Brief or fragmented mention of what's coming, without sequencing or framing.

bands.label: Fail
bands.criteria: No upfront structure. Launches into random topics. Client has no sense of where the call is going.

positiveSignals: Sequenced coverage ("connect, get aligned on your goals, walk you through the journey, support, schedule next") — numbered or natural-language
negativeSignals: Client doesn't know where the call is going
notes: A coach who says "we've got 30 minutes — connect, get aligned on your goals, what success looks like, walk you through the journey, get clear on support, and schedule the next call" is delivering Elite-level agenda framing even without numbered enumeration. Score 4.5–5, not 3.

Numbered enumeration is NOT required. A sequenced delivery that covers at least three distinct phases of the call (e.g. "first… then… and finally…", or comma/and-connected items) qualifies as structured if it is paired with explicit time framing and at least implicit client buy-in.

Calibration note: A coach who says "we've got 30 minutes — connect, get aligned on your goals, what success looks like, walk you through the journey, get clear on support, and schedule the next call" is delivering Elite-level agenda framing even without numbered enumeration. Score 4.5–5, not 3.

dimensions.title: Goal Alignment & Deep Why
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach go beyond functional goals to uncover the emotional/identity driver? Is a North Star statement built?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Extracts emotional drivers + clear 30-day success metrics. ≥2 follow-up questions on "why". Extracts emotional/identity driver (fear, family, legacy, career, self-image). Builds a North Star statement: "What I hear you saying is you want to be the active husband and father you envision for decades to come." Defines specific 30-day success metric. Client verbally confirms ("Yes, that's exactly it").

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Understands goals but stays surface level. 1 follow-up + some emotional context. 30-day goal vague or not established. North Star implied but not solidified. Physical goals identified, not emotionally deep.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Mostly repeats sales notes. Asks "what are your goals?" and accepts the first answer. Stays physical only ("lose weight", "more flexible"). No probing, no emotional depth, no North Star.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No meaningful alignment. Reads from sales notes without engagement. Skips or rushes. Accepts generic answer ("I want to be healthy") and moves on.

positiveSignals: "What would make day 30 feel like the best investment you've ever made?"
negativeSignals: Accepts "I want to be healthy" without digging
Never references the goal later in the call.
notes: #1 loss dimension per Marcus's analysis: Most coaches stay surface on the "why". They visit the goal but never strengthen the connection to the North Star.

dimensions.title: Program Explanation (3 Phases)
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the client leave understanding the 3-phase structure and why it exists?

bands.label: Elite
bands.criteria: All 3 phases clearly named (in any equivalent phrasing) with outcomes for each. Uses an analogy (pyramid, mountain, ladder) or reassessment cadence ("week 4, 8, 12, 16"). Each phase tied to the client's specific goal. High belief transfer — client understands WHY the path is structured this way.

bands.label: Strong
bands.criteria: All 3 phases clearly identified in correct order (with any naming), but delivery is simple or moderately generic. Phases may not be deeply tied to the client's specific goals, OR analogy / reassessment cadence is missing, OR the coach does not explicitly check client understanding. Score 8 when phases are crisp and complete; 6 when phases are present but explanation is brief.

bands.label: Mid
bands.criteria: Fragmented explanation. 1–2 phases mentioned vaguely, or the progression is implied but not laid out in sequence. Client may not clearly understand the journey.

bands.label: Weak
bands.criteria: Only references to "phases" or "steps" without naming or sequencing.

bands.label: Fail
bands.criteria: Skips or misrepresents. No phase explanation at all. Just "we'll do mobility exercises."

positiveSignals: "Movement Retraining → Remodeling → Integrating" (or any equivalent phrasing in correct order)
Phases linked to client's specific goal
Coach asks client if it makes sense.
negativeSignals: Phases named but not in the correct sequence
notes: When a coach uses "Movement Retraining → Remodeling → Integrating" — that is the correct Halden Method naming. Credit it as Elite-tier phase identification. Do NOT drop the score because the labels don't say "Reset/Build/Freedom".

Halden Method 3-phase canon: **(1) Movement Retraining** — restore foundational movement quality, address asymmetries, retrain core patterns. **(2) Movement Remodeling** — load and rebuild new patterns into strength. **(3) Movement Integrating** — integrate full-capacity movement into life and sport.

Naming flexibility: Accept ANY phrasing that conveys the three-stage progression in correct order. Legacy synonyms include Reset/Baseline → Build/Strength → Freedom/Mastery, or any equivalent (e.g. "rebuild the foundation → load the pattern → free movement"). Do NOT penalize a coach for using the canonical Retraining/Remodeling/Integrating naming.

Calibration note: When a coach uses "Movement Retraining → Remodeling → Integrating" — that is the correct Halden Method naming. Credit it as Elite-tier phase identification. Do NOT drop the score because the labels don't say "Reset/Build/Freedom".

dimensions.title: Journey & Expectation Setting
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach prepare the client emotionally for the difficulty of the journey?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Clearly explains milestones, timeline, challenges. Normalizes emotional friction explicitly: "There will be a week where you feel like you're not progressing — that's normal." Explains valleys (weeks 3–4). Distinguishes good discomfort from bad pain. Explains the first month is foundational, not transformational. Links back to North Star: "When we're at week 8, I'll ask if you feel like you're becoming…"

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Covers basics but misses emotional prep. Timeline explained, structure ok. Normalizes physical discomfort but not emotional. Missing psychological preparation for valleys.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Vague expectations. Informative but not experiential. Explains what will happen but not how it will feel. Sounds instructional, not coaching.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No expectation setting. Leaves client with unrealistic expectations. Doesn't mention that there will be hard moments.

positiveSignals: "Around week 3–4 you might feel in a valley"
"It's normal to feel overwhelmed — I want you to reach out when that happens."
negativeSignals: Only positivity, no mention of difficulty
notes: #2 loss dimension per Marcus's analysis: Most coaches explain the timeline but never normalize emotional friction. Clients hit week 3–4 unprepared and disengage.

dimensions.title: Support System Clarity
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach communicate, in this call, exactly how the client will be supported between sessions — primary channel, response expectations, community access, and how accountability will work?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Clearly explains all channels + when to use each. Primary channel named explicitly ("the training app is our main channel for daily check-ins"). Response time stated ("I respond within 24h"). the community platform/community access mentioned and how to use it. Accountability style asked or framed ("Do you want me to push you, or to stay in the background?"). Client visibly understands how to reach the coach and what to expect.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Mentions support but unclear usage. Channel mentioned but no response times. Vague "reach out anytime" without structure. No accountability framing.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Not explained. No mention of how the client reaches the coach between sessions. No channel named. No response expectations.

positiveSignals: "the training app is our main channel"
"the community platform community is where the cohort lives"
"Do you want me to push you or stay back?"
negativeSignals: No mention of the training app

dimensions.title: Coaching Intelligence Questions
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach gather information that goes beyond logistics into behavioral patterns, psychology, and personalization?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Asks key behavioral + self-awareness questions. Asks about behavioral patterns ("What has stopped you in the past?"). Probes consistency triggers ("What usually throws you off a program?"). Asks about learning style ("How do you learn best — do you need to be pushed or supported?"). Asks about stress response. Uses answers to personalize coaching approach. Identifies client archetype signals (Doer / Controller / Worrier / Follower).

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Asks 1–2 but lacks depth. Asks about pain triggers, schedule, training style. Missing behavioral pattern or mindset questions. Doesn't use answers to adapt approach.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Generic questions only. Basic questions only (frequency, equipment, availability). Surface-level coaching. Doesn't use answers to adapt.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Skipped. No coaching intelligence questions. Only "when are you available?" and "do you have equipment?" Client not truly known.

positiveSignals: "How do you respond when you're overwhelmed?"
"Do you prefer I push you or support gently?"
"What usually makes you quit a program?"
notes: Archetype detection signals: Doer = confident, data-driven, wants "the how". Controller = pushes back, questions the process, needs proof. Worrier = seeks reassurance, doubts themselves, asks "what if". Follower = enthusiastic but vague goals, history of not following through.

dimensions.title: Next Steps & Diagnostics
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the client leave knowing exactly what to do and when?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Clear, confident, client understands exactly what to do. Pipeline: diagnostics → film → upload → program → start date. Explains how to film videos (angle, device). Removes all confusion with demo or screen share. Time specified ("send by Saturday, program Monday"). Client verbally confirms they understand.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Some clarity but minor confusion. Clear instructions but no demo. Timeline ok but slightly rushed. Minor ambiguity but overall strong clarity.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Vague instructions. Partially clear, some gaps. Client has unresolved doubts. No specific timeline.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No clear next steps. "I'll send you some stuff" without explanation. Client doesn't know what to do after the call. No structure.

positiveSignals: "Here's what you do: open the training app, find diagnostics, film, upload"
"Send by Saturday, you'll have your program by Monday"
negativeSignals: Client asks "So what do I do now?"
notes: #3 loss dimension per Marcus's analysis: "I'll send you some stuff" is the most expensive sentence in coaching. Vague next steps lose clients in the hand-off.

dimensions.title: Booking Next Call
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Is the next call booked LIVE before the call ends?

bands.label: Elite
bands.criteria: Date and time confirmed verbally during the call. Coach navigates the client's scheduling constraints live (time zones, weekly availability, conflicts). Score 5 when booking is crisp and the coach proactively closes it; 4.5 when booking is confirmed but slightly rushed or with minor ambiguity.

bands.label: Mid
bands.criteria: Attempted but not fully secured. Coach raises booking but leaves excessive flexibility ("I'll send you a link", "we'll organize via message") rather than locking date + time live.

bands.label: Weak
bands.criteria: Booking referenced only in passing, with no concrete attempt to lock it during the call.

bands.label: Fail
bands.criteria: Not addressed. Call ends without any mention of the next call.

positiveSignals: "Let's book it now before we close"
Resolves scheduling conflict live ("you're 13 hours ahead, so for you that's…")
notes: If date and time are confirmed verbally and any time-zone / scheduling friction is resolved live, score 5/5 — even if the transcript does not explicitly confirm that the calendar invite was sent during the recording.

Booking is verbal, not technical. The substantive test is verbal confirmation of date and time during the call. Whether the calendar invite is technically clicked on-screen during the call versus immediately after is an artifact of the recording — it is NOT a deduction.

Calibration note: If date and time are confirmed verbally and any time-zone / scheduling friction is resolved live, score 5/5 — even if the transcript does not explicitly confirm that the calendar invite was sent during the recording.

dimensions.title: Close, Recap & Confidence
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the call end with energy, structure, and an emotional anchor — not just logistics?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Strong recap, reinforces confidence. Structured recap: "Here's what we covered today: X, Y, Z." Confidence anchor: "You're in the right place" / "You're exactly the type of person who succeeds here." Emotional reinforcement: excitement for the journey. Does NOT end with only logistics.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Basic close. Positive close but no structured recap. Generic encouragement without emotional anchor. Ends with next steps logistically. Or flat close: "Ok, talk soon."

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Abrupt or unclear ending. Call ends in a disappointing or flat way. Client leaves without feeling excited.

positiveSignals: "I'm excited about this journey with you."

dimensions.title: Post-Call Execution
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach commit, in-call, to specific post-call deliverables with concrete deadlines? This dimension scores **what is said in the call** — verification of actual delivery is out of QC scope until the training app + the video tool integration is live.

bands.label: Elite
bands.criteria: Multiple explicit post-call commitments with precise deadlines: recap timing ("recap within 10 minutes"), diagnostics assigned live ("assigning your diagnostics in the training app now"), program delivery date stated ("program loaded by Monday"). All time-bound. Score 5 when 3+ commitments with crisp timing; 4.5 when 2+ commitments with precise timing.

bands.label: Strong
bands.criteria: Two or more post-call commitments with mostly precise timing — minor gaps (one commitment with rougher timing, or one specific commitment plus one general one).

bands.label: Mid
bands.criteria: At least one specific commitment, but timing is rough or only one or two commitments are made. Includes informal-but-real commitments like "I'll get diagnostics done over the weekend". Partial in-call promise hygiene.

bands.label: Weak
bands.criteria: Vague reference to follow-up ("I'll send you stuff") without specific deliverable or timing.

bands.label: Fail
bands.criteria: No post-call commitments stated at all. Call ends with no clarity on what the coach will do next.

positiveSignals: "I'll send you the recap in the next 10–15 minutes"
"Your program will be ready by Monday"
Specific or implied timing on every commitment
notes: A commitment like "I'll get the diagnostics done over the weekend" is real but soft — score it as Mid (2–3), not Fail (0).

Informal commitments still count. A specific commitment with implied or rough timing (e.g. "I'll get your diagnostics done over the weekend") is a real promise — score it in the Mid band, not Fail. Reserve Fail for calls where the coach makes no commitment at all.
Calibration note: A commitment like "I'll get the diagnostics done over the weekend" is real but soft — score it as Mid (2–3), not Fail (0).

caps.condition: No follow-up questions anywhere in the call
caps.raw: No follow-up questions anywhere in the call → Max 70 total

caps.condition: Coach speaks >70% of the time without client engagement
caps.raw: Coach speaks >70% of the time without client engagement → Max 80 total

caps.condition: Client shows unresolved confusion at any point
caps.raw: Client shows unresolved confusion at any point → Max 75 total
No North Star statement constructed → Max 10/15 on Dimension 4

bands.name: ELITE
bands.description: Deep + clear + client confirms. Coach builds real human relationship, not just process.

bands.name: STRONG
bands.description: Clear and useful but lacks emotional depth or consistent reinforcement.

bands.name: INCONSISTENT
bands.description: Technically correct but generic or surface-level in key areas.

bands.name: AT RISK
bands.description: Weak client experience. Client may be doubting the program.

bands.name: FAIL
bands.description: Missed core elements, major retention risk.

preamble: **Scope.** Transcript only, all twelve dimensions active. D7 (support system
clarity) and D12 (post-call execution) are scored on what is communicated
during the call, not on whether the follow-up actually landed afterwards.
**Band-based scoring.** Each dimension's score must fall inside one of the
bands listed in its table. Within a band, any integer works (or a half step
where the dimension's max is 5 or less) depending on how close the call sits
to the next band up. A call that clearly exceeds the Mid criteria but does not
fully meet Elite belongs in the Strong band. Rounding down to Mid needs a
principles: **Every score is based on 3 things:** depth (how far the coach goes), clarity (how well it lands), and client response (did it actually land).
**If it doesn't land → it cannot score elite.** A perfect explanation that the client didn't confirm is not elite.
**Quote-first rationale.** Every rationale must begin with a direct or paraphrased reference to something that happened in the transcript. Never score from impressions.

**Conservative on missing evidence — within the band.** If a behavior cannot be verified in the transcript, score in the lower tier of the band the call belongs to. This is NOT a license to drop into a lower band entirely. If the call clearly exceeds Mid criteria but you cannot verify every Elite element, score in the Strong band (lower tier) — do not collapse to Mid.

**The four-sentiment test.** Before finalizing each score, ask whether the client would leave the call feeling: 1. "This coach gets me" 2. "I know exactly what to do next" 3. "I trust this process" 4. "I'm excited to start"
calibrationAnchors: D1 — credit content over disclosure. | Coach references the client's specific goals + injuries from the sales call but does NOT say "I read your notes" → Strong (7–8), not Mid. The conduct is the test, not the disclosure. | Coach is otherwise well-prepared but makes one factual misstep (e.g. wrong city) → Strong (6–7), not Mid. A single error in an otherwise solid opening is not a band drop. | Coach lets the client share context voluntarily for connection / relational warmth → not a deduction. This is an intentional technique, not a preparation failure.

D3 — natural agenda phrasing is Elite. | Coach says "we've got 30 minutes — connect, get aligned on your goals, what success looks like, walk you through the journey, get clear on support, and schedule the next call" → 4.5–5, not 3. Sequenced delivery + time framing + ≥3 phases qualifies as structured, even without numbered enumeration.

D5 — accept the canonical Halden Method naming. | Coach explains "Movement Retraining → Movement Remodeling → Movement Integrating" → credit as fully-named 3-phase explanation. Score in Strong–Elite range based on depth, analogies, and tie-to-goals — NOT based on whether the labels match "Reset/Build/Freedom".

D10 — verbal booking is Elite. | Coach confirms specific date and time verbally and resolves time-zone or scheduling friction live → 5/5, even if the transcript does not explicitly verify the calendar invite was sent during the recording.

D12 — informal commitments are Mid, not Fail. | "I'll get your diagnostics done over the weekend" → 2–3, not 0. Commitment exists with implied timing; it is real even if soft. Reserve 0 for the absence of any commitment whatsoever.
